question.problem: In a factory, the cost of producing an item depends on the number of items produced per day. The function $U(x)$ models the cost, in dollars, to produce an item if the factory is producing $x$ items per day. What is the best interpretation of ${U}^{′}(500)=0.01?$
question.worked_solution:
The function ${U}^{′}(x)$ represents the rate at which the cost changes when the factory produces $x$ items per day. 

Therefore, ${U}^{′}(500)=0.01$ means:

$\,$ *When the factory produces $500$ items per day, the cost per item increases at a rate of $0.01$ dollars per item*
